Using the listed base and sign-on estimates, **B is ahead by 2,000 over 12 months; A is ahead by 9,000 over 24 months**, after housing and moving costs and before tax.

These are prospective scenarios, not offers. All figures are fictional currency units. This assumes full employment from day one, evenly paid base, sign-on at the start, recurring monthly housing, and one moving payment.

| Listed cash and costs | A: 12 months | B: 12 months | A: 24 months | B: 24 months |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Base | 120,000 | 115,000 | 240,000 | 230,000 |
| One-time sign-on | 10,000 | 20,000 | 10,000 | 20,000 |
| Housing | −24,000 | −30,000 | −48,000 | −60,000 |
| One-time moving cost | −5,000 | −2,000 | −5,000 | −2,000 |
| **Cash after listed costs** | **101,000** | **103,000** | **197,000** | **188,000** |

Formula: `annual base × months / 12 + sign-on − monthly housing × months − moving cost`.

A has 96,000 in annual base after housing, versus B’s 85,000. That recurring 11,000 advantage eventually outweighs B’s larger upfront net cash. Neither sign-on nor moving costs are repeated in year two.

**Bonus is separate.** A’s 20,000 target is discretionary; its cadence and payment dates are not supplied. B’s bonus is unspecified, not known to be zero. If A paid 20,000 once by month 12 and again by month 24, its totals would be 121,000 and 237,000. Against B’s listed-cash baseline, those are leads of 18,000 and 49,000, but that illustration assumes those payouts and excludes any unknown B bonus. More generally, A needs over 2,000 more bonus cash than B to lead at 12 months; B needs over 9,000 more than A to lead at 24 months.

**Private equity stays outside cash.** A’s 50,000 is an illiquid paper quote, with instrument, vesting and realization terms unknown. It contributes no spendable cash to these scenarios. B’s equity is unspecified. Do not double A’s paper quote for the 24-month horizon.

This covers only the listed pay, housing and moving costs. Taxes, other living expenses, benefits, raises and any unknown terms are excluded, so it is not a complete savings forecast.
